title: Don't let llama-cpp-python failures block install (#1)
paragraphs: llama-cpp-python has no prebuilt PyPI wheel, so it needs a C/C++ compiler to build from source. It only backs the optional, off-by- default transcript formatter, so a failed build there was aborting the whole install and blocking core dictation on any machine without a compiler (confirmed on a Windows ARM64 VM with no VS Build Tools).
deps.ps1 now warns and continues when an optional package fails instead of throwing. Added tests/windows/deps.Tests.ps1 covering both the optional-failure and required-failure paths.

title: Wait for the target app to read the paste
paragraphs: The old clipboard was restored 100ms after Cmd+V. A busy app (Claude or ChatGPT mid-stream) could read the clipboard after that and paste the old contents or nothing, while the log still said the text was injected.

The text is now offered through a lazy pasteboard provider, so the old clipboard only comes back after the target reads it. If it never reads it within 2s, Voice Type plays a sound and leaves the text on the clipboard. The log records how long each target took to read.

title: Don't reuse an old py2app applet as the approved launcher
paragraphs: Upgrading a machine that still ran the py2app 'Voice Type.app' saved that applet as the trusted launcher, and it cannot host the current runtime, so the worker never became ready. Both setup_mac.sh and the launch wrapper now only honour native launchers.

title: Add Restart button to voice-type settings window
paragraphs: A last-resort recovery for a wedged overlay. In the deadlocks we've seen, only the hotkey/streamer threads hang — the tkinter UI thread stays alive — so the settings window is still usable and can trigger a restart.

The button (next to Open Log) confirms, then spawns the platform relauncher (voice-type-mac.sh / restart.bat) detached with start_new_session so it survives this process being killed. The relauncher kills the current process — clearing the stuck overlay — and starts a fresh instance.

title: Self-heal: a fresh launch reclaims a wedged voice-type instance
paragraphs: If voice-type deadlocks (e.g. the CoreAudio stream-close hang), its hotkey loop stops and pressing F12 does nothing — the only recovery was manually finding and killing the process.

Now the hotkey loop refreshes a heartbeat file ~2x/sec. On launch, if another instance holds the single-instance lock:
- fresh heartbeat  -> it's healthy, exit as a duplicate (as before)
- stale/absent (>10s) -> it's wedged: SIGTERM (then SIGKILL) that pid and take over the lock.
So recovery from a deadlock is just re-running the launcher / menubar restart — the new instance evicts the zombie automatically. Verified with both a healthy-duplicate and a SIGSTOP-wedged instance.

title: Make voice-type resilient to CoreAudio deadlock on stream close
paragraphs: A debugger attach on a wedged instance showed recorder.stop() deadlocked inside CoreAudio: the hotkey thread was in PortAudio's stream stop (AudioOutputUnitStop -> HALB_Mutex) while the CoreAudio IO thread held the opposing lock. recorder.stop() never returned, so streamer.stop() on the next line never ran and the preview loop transcribed forever, pegging CPU with the overlay stuck on "REC".

- Run the stream stop/close on a throwaway thread with a 2s timeout (STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT). A CoreAudio deadlock now leaks one thread instead of wedging the whole app; the next _ensure_stream() opens a fresh stream.
- Stop the streaming preview loop before recorder.stop() in the key-up handler, so even a hung stop can't leave the overlay/CPU spinning.

title: Fix voice-type hotkey getting stuck down and pegging CPU
paragraphs: The F12 push-to-talk state is tracked via a macOS CGEventTap. macOS auto-disables a tap if its callback is judged too slow, after which no further events (including the F12 KeyUp) arrive — leaving the hotkey stuck "down" so recording never stops and the stream loop re-transcribes the same buffer forever.

- Handle kCGEventTapDisabledByTimeout/ByUserInput: re-enable the tap and reset the hotkey state.
- Move the frontmost-app snapshot off the tap callback into the main worker (snapshot_target_app) so slow AppKit calls can't trip the tap watchdog.
- Add a 120s max-recording safety cap so a stuck key self-recovers.
- Guard StreamingTranscriber.start() against double-start, which spawned a second loop thread and doubled every log line.
- Harden voice-type-mac.sh to wait for the old instance to exit and escalate to SIGKILL, so a wedged process can't coexist with a new one.

title: Add NVIDIA Parakeet backend + GPU support
paragraphs:
- Add NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6b via sherpa-onnx as an alternative final model - runs offline transducer inference on CPU with INT8 quantization, very fast for short clips
- Add PyTorch cu128 DLL path registration at startup so ctranslate2 can find cublas64_12.dll without needing the CUDA Toolkit on PATH
- Whisper models now use GPU (CUDA) when available
- Add filler word stripping for Parakeet output (uh, um, er, ah, hmm etc.)
- Add user-editable corrections dict in settings.json for fixing model misrecognitions (e.g. Q DA -> CUDA)
- Prefix model names in tray menu with provider (Whisper / NVIDIA Parakeet)
- Force final_only output mode when Parakeet is selected
- Add output mode menu (final_only / hybrid / stabilized / precompute) and supporting finalize helpers for Whisper workflows
Made-with: Cursor

Add model selector, fix audio cutoff at start
paragraphs:
Model selector:
- Add settings.json persistence (gitignored) with final_model and stream_model keys; auto-created on first run with hardware-appropriate defaults (large-v3-turbo on CUDA, small.en on CPU)
- Final Model submenu in tray: tiny.en, base.en, small.en, medium.en, large-v2, large-v3, large-v3-turbo (radio-button style)
- Preview Model submenu: tiny.en, base.en, small.en
- Hot-swap: picking a model reloads it in the background, no restart needed
- Fix pystray crash: action lambdas with default args (3 co_argcount) are rejected by pystray; use factory functions to capture loop vars instead

Audio cutoff fix:
- Keep the InputStream open permanently rather than opening/closing it on each keypress; Windows microphone hardware activation was dropping the first 100-300ms of every recording
- Reduce blocksize from 1024 to 256 (64ms -> 16ms per callback) so capture starts within one block of the key going down
- Recording is gated by a _recording flag in the callback instead

title: Fix kill reliability, add restart.bat, fix preview scrolling
paragraphs:
- voice-type.ps1: switch from Get-WmiObject to Get-CimInstance for killing existing instances (Get-WmiObject silently returns nothing on Win10/11 because CommandLine is null via that provider)
- restart.bat: new dev script that kills all instances then relaunches via vbs, analogous to taskmon's build-and-run.bat - always use this instead of launching python directly
- voice-type.py: _wrap_preview now shows the last 2 lines instead of the first 2, so the overlay tracks what you're currently saying when recording long clips (earlier text scrolls off with a leading ellipsis)
- AGENTS.md: update voice-type dev workflow to reference restart.bat

title: Inject text via SendInput instead of clipboard
paragraphs: Replaces pyperclip + Ctrl+V with SendInput using KEYEVENTF_UNICODE flags, so transcribed text is injected directly into the focused window without touching the clipboard. Removes pyperclip dependency.

title: docs: split README into per-tool READMEs, add ghopen README; voice-type waveform animation and streaming improvements
Add push-to-talk local voice transcription tool
paragraphs: Hold Right Ctrl to record, release to transcribe and paste into the active window. Features: faster-whisper backend (small.en on CPU, large-v3-turbo on CUDA), live streaming preview overlay, system tray mic icon with enable/disable and run-on-startup toggle, GetAsyncKeyState polling (no global hook), log auto-rotates at 1 MB. Also adds *.log to .gitignore.
